title: Spectrophotometer

references.label: General microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)

purpose: Measures the absorbance (or transmittance) of light through a liquid sample at a specified wavelength, commonly used to estimate bacterial culture density (optical density, OD) or determine solute concentration via the Beer-Lambert relationship.
operatingPrinciple: Light of a selected wavelength passes through a cuvette containing the sample; a detector measures how much light is transmitted versus absorbed. Absorbance relates to concentration and path length through the Beer-Lambert law (see the Beer-Lambert Formula and Calculator), but a direct concentration reading is only valid within the instrument's linear range and after appropriate calibration/blanking.
basicOperation: Select the appropriate wavelength for the measurement (e.g. 600 nm is commonly used for bacterial culture turbidity, though the exact wavelength convention can vary by lab/protocol).
Blank the instrument using the appropriate blank (e.g. sterile uninoculated medium) at the same wavelength before reading samples.
Use clean, scratch-free, matched cuvettes and avoid air bubbles or fingerprints in the light path.
Dilute samples that read above the instrument's linear range rather than trusting an out-of-range reading.
importantSettings: Cuvette path length (commonly 1 cm, but must match what any conversion or standard curve assumes)
calibration: Periodic wavelength accuracy and photometric accuracy checks per the manufacturer's schedule, typically using certified reference filters or solutions; verify a fresh blank before each measurement session.
maintenance: Keep the cuvette chamber clean and free of spills.
Store cuvettes properly to avoid scratches, which scatter light and distort readings.

commonErrors.problem: Unexpectedly high or erratic absorbance readings
commonErrors.cause: Air bubbles, fingerprints, or scratches on the cuvette; or a sample outside the instrument's linear range
commonErrors.fix: Re-clean/replace the cuvette and re-check for bubbles; dilute the sample and re-measure if it was likely off-scale

commonErrors.cause: Instrument not re-blanked, or lamp warm-up not complete
commonErrors.fix: Re-blank with fresh reference solution and allow the recommended warm-up time before starting a measurement series

safety: Handle cuvettes containing biological samples with the same precautions as the culture itself.
Dispose of used cuvettes and samples per the applicable biosafety and chemical waste procedures.
